Bandza Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Bandza, Georgia

Not demolished. Bandza's Jewish community, in Georgia's Samegrelo region, traces to the second half of the 18th century, likely migrating from Lailashi. By the 19th century, the village had grown into an important western Georgian trading center with about 250 Jewish families, who held exclusive local trading rights by mid-century. Two brick synagogues were built in the early 20th century (Sepiashvili, 1910; Ajiashvili, 1915), and a Zionist organization formed in the community's first quarter of the century, sending representatives to Georgia's 1919 Zionist conference. Population peaked around 650 in 1939, supported partly by a Jewish collective farm in the 1920s-30s, before collapsing to just 20 Jews by 1979 and 2 families by the 1990s as most residents emigrated to Israel. This cemetery's earliest legible tombstone dates to 1898; it remained in use until 1994, when it effectively became inactive as the community departed.
